title: Classical Test Theory (CTT): Model, Error Types, Reliability, Assumptions
summary: CTT model (observed score = true score + error); types of error; reliability in CTT; standard error of measurement; key assumptions.
objectives: State the CTT model X = T + E.
revision: CTT: X = T + E. Reliability r_xx = σ²_T / σ²_X. Assumptions: linear, uncorrelated errors, E(E)=0, E(X)=T.
traps: X = T + E — memorise the CTT equation.
confusions: Confusing CTT with IRT (item-level vs test-level).

notes.t: A measurement model expressing observed score as the sum of true score and random error: X = T + E.
X = observed score, T = true score (the score the person would get with perfect measurement), E = random error. The true score is the average of observed scores over infinite repetitions.

i: Random error: unpredictable fluctuations that average to zero over repetitions.
Systematic error: consistent bias that does not average to zero.

notes.t: The proportion of observed score variance that is true score variance: r_xx = σ²_T / σ²_X.

i: Uncorrelated errors: E is uncorrelated with T and with other errors.
True score is the expected observed score: E(X) = T.

notes.t:
Worked example: Observed score variance σ²_X = 100, true score variance σ²_T = 70.
Reliability r_xx = σ²_T / σ²_X = 70 / 100 = 0.70.
Interpretation: 70% of observed score variance is true variance; 30% is error variance.
CTT formula X = T + E and reliability r_xx = σ²_T / σ²_X are frequently tested in UGC NET psychometric questions.

mnemonics.title: XTE
mnemonics.text: X = T + E: Observed = True + Error

flashcards.a: r_xx = σ²_T / σ²_X (true variance / observed variance).
